habitat: Pairs, often in bird parties, in the canopy of large trees in woodland, riverine bush and evergreen forest fringes.
summary: A common resident. A small pied bird. The eyes are crimson, orange or yellow. The female has a white forehead and eyebrow, and both sexes have wing-barring. An excited male puffs out the white back feathers and may fly like that while calling chick-weeu. The wings make a purring sound in a heavy flight. The Kemp code RB was left unchanged.

viewNotes.note: Small pied bird. The eyes may be crimson, orange or yellow, so no single iris colour is stored.
Pied front. Newman does not itemise the black and white parts of the male head.
Pied back. When excited the male puffs the white back feathers.
Heavy flight, the wings making a purring sound, with wing-barring. The male may fly with the back puffed.

Pied, with a white forehead and eyebrow, and wing-barring.
Pied back and barred wings. The white puff is described for the male.

calls.description: A sharp chick-weeu, chick-weeu, given while flying with the back puffed, and less often while feeding. Grade A call from near Sabie Park, Bushbuckridge. The filename is XC368159-170328_Black-backedPuffback_SabiePark_OC.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, so status is resident and all twelve months are listed. The eye is crimson, orange or yellow, so the iris token is left blank. Pied areas are not split into black and white tokens. Population figures and the Kemp code RB were left unchanged.
